steps.note: One step. Off-days and holidays in the range are excluded and not consumed by the leave (BR-6, BR-12), and a request raised by the student is held until the guardian endorses it (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A missing document for long sick leave, dates out of order, a range with no working day, dates outside the student's enrolment and an overlap with existing leave are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the request, its dates and the guardian's reason, together with the audit entry or not at all. **Nothing is excused yet** — the student is still marked absent on those days until the request is approved (BR-5). Where the student raised it, it is held for the guardian's endorsement and does not reach the Coordinator (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. It is what the Coordinator weighs (BR-2), and a reason a planner wrote describes what it inferred about a family's circumstances rather than what they said.
Never choose the leave type to avoid a document. The type decides whether one is required (BR-4), and recording a fortnight's illness as Family leave to get past E1 misstates why a child was away.

Never describe the request as excusing the absence. Nothing is excused until it is approved (BR-2, BR-5) — the child is still marked absent on those days meanwhile, and the family will assume otherwise.

Report the days actually counted and the dates excluded. Off-days and holidays inside the range are not consumed (BR-6, BR-12), so a Friday-to-Monday request may count two days rather than four — and the family should know which.

Never endorse a student's own request. A request raised by a student is held until the guardian endorses it, and only then does it reach the Coordinator — a student must not be able to authorise their own absence (BR-3).
Report the frequency flag rather than treating it as a refusal. Repeated requests are flagged to the Coordinator rather than blocked, because a family with a genuinely ill child asks often (BR-11).

reversal.statement: A submitted request is approved, rejected or cancelled by the guardian before it starts (BR-10); nothing here withdraws one. No attendance mark has changed and nothing is excused.

routesElsewhere.note: The decision is notified as part of the approval.

steps.note: One step, and it reaches the attendance record. On each approved leave day the student is marked as approved leave automatically, so whoever marks that section sees it already applied (BR-5).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A student request without endorsement, and an overlap with leave already approved, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the approval, a leave mark on each working day covered, any amendment to a day already marked absent, and the audit entry together or not at all. Whoever marks that section's attendance sees the mark already applied and does not have to remember (BR-5). Approved leave suppresses the absence alert for those days and is counted separately from unexplained absence (BR-7). Where a day was already marked absent, the attendance record is amended with the reason kept (BR-9) — the original mark stays visible.
